title: A callable is not assignable to Closure, although a Closure is a callable

ground_truth.statement: PHP's callable pseudo-type covers closures, strings and arrays, while \Closure is one class. A value that is only known to be callable is therefore not assignable to a \Closure parameter: 'phpversion' is callable but is not an instance of Closure, and both from_string_literal() and from_callable('strlen') throw a TypeError when they reach keep(). The asymmetric control is a real closure, which is accepted and returns.

notes: A green row kept as a regression guard: all three analyzers separate callable from Closure and report both the literal string (line 19, a definite violation) and the callable-typed parameter (line 14, where the value may be a string), while line 24 - an actual closure - stays silent for all three. The runtime script also shows that 'phpversion' really is usable as a callable (is_callable and call_user_func), so the case is about the class boundary, not about callability. Psalm calls the line-14 report ArgumentTypeCoercion rather than InvalidArgument, which is its own code for a coerced argument; that is a naming difference, not a disagreement about the fact.

sources.note: same callable-Must-be-reconciled-as-a-union theme; this fixture is a clean-room rewrite about the Closure boundary
